description: Web development company London firms trust with redesigns, migrations that keep rankings, e-commerce and client portals. Meet the team in London.
h1: A web development company London firms trust with the site that pays
intro: 22 Signals is a web development company London firms hire for websites, e-commerce stores and client portals. We work with established businesses in law, finance, retail, property and healthcare. Every build is fast, accessible, ready for UK cookie and privacy rules, and made to rank in Google and show up in AI answers from launch day.

sections.h: When the website stops pulling its weight
p: Firms usually come to us with one of three problems. The site looks dated next to competitors who rebuilt last year. The site looks fine but brings in few enquiries, because it loads slowly on a phone and search engines struggle to read it. Or the business has outgrown it: clients want to log in, upload documents, pay an invoice or book online, and the current platform cannot do any of that without plugins held together with tape.

A new design alone fixes the first problem. The other two need a team that understands search, content, hosting, integrations and conversion as well as layout. That is the kind of web development company London buyers should be looking for, and it is the way we work.

We also meet a fourth group: firms that rebuilt recently and watched enquiries fall, because the new site dropped pages that ranked or broke the redirects. Recovering from that is slower than avoiding it, which is why migration planning is the part of a project we refuse to rush.

sections.h: UK rules your website has to follow
p: A London website carries more legal weight than people expect. Cookie banners must ask before setting non-essential cookies under PECR and UK GDPR, and the ICO has been clear that rejecting should be as easy as accepting. Privacy notices have to match what the site actually collects. The Equality Act 2010 means private businesses should not shut out disabled users, and building to WCAG 2.2 AA is the practical way to meet that.

Some sectors have their own requirements. Firms regulated by the SRA must display the SRA clickable badge, and many have to publish price and service information under the SRA Transparency Rules. FCA-authorised firms need any financial promotion on the site approved and kept compliant. Online shops must give the cancellation and returns information consumer law requires. We build these in from the start, and your compliance lead checks the wording.

sections.h: How a project runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: a short call about what the site needs to achieve and what is holding the current one back. Plan: a written scope with a sitemap, content plan, technical choices and, for redesigns, a full URL map so nothing that ranks is lost. Build: design, development and content, shown to you in stages on a staging site. Grow: launch, then we watch search data, fix anything that dips and improve the pages that bring enquiries.
Every date goes in writing, including the launch date, and your Signal Lead owns all of them.

We built a client portal for a US law firm where clients log in, exchange documents and pay invoices online, replacing a mix of email attachments and phone payments. The same approach suits London firms whose clients expect to manage their matter, account or booking without calling the office.

For London clients we can hold the kick-off and the design review in person, and you can bring the partners or directors who need to approve the look. Seeing a design on a big screen with the decision makers in the room saves weeks of email.

Between those meetings, progress is shared on a staging site, and every change is tested there before it reaches you. Releases go live in agreed windows, never on a Friday afternoon, which matters for e-commerce and for firms whose clients use the site in New York or the Gulf.

sections.h: How to choose a web development company: London checklist
list: Ask how they protect rankings during a redesign, and ask to see a URL redirect map
Check whether they build to WCAG 2.2 AA, or just say the site is accessible
Find out who writes and checks the content, not just who designs the pages
Ask what happens after launch: who patches the site, monitors uptime and answers the phone
Make sure you own the domain, hosting account and code

p: We quote after scoping, because sites vary widely. The main factors:
list: Number of page templates and the amount of content to write or move
E-commerce, booking, portal or payment features
Integrations with CRMs, practice management or stock systems
Migration complexity and the number of URLs to map
Accessibility testing and any sector compliance requirements
Ongoing care and hosting after launch

p: A website is one part of how a firm wins clients. Because the same team runs SEO and GEO (generative engine optimisation), paid media, video and AI tools, your site is built to work with all of them: landing pages ready for campaigns, video that loads fast, an enquiry form that feeds an AI assistant or your CRM. If you are planning a rebuild, book a 15-minute call and we will tell you honestly whether you need one. Related London pages: SEO and GEO, app development and paid media.

faqs.q: Can you redesign our site without losing Google rankings?
faqs.a: Yes. We crawl the current site, map every URL that ranks or has links to its new address, keep the content that performs, set up redirects and test them before launch. After launch we watch Search Console and fix anything that drops. Most rankings carry over when migrations are planned this carefully.

faqs.q: Do you meet clients in person in London?
faqs.a: Yes. We usually hold the kick-off and the main design review in person, at your office or a meeting room nearby. That is where the important decisions get made. Day-to-day progress is shared on a staging site with weekly updates from your Signal Lead.

faqs.q: Which platform should a London business use?
faqs.a: It depends on who will edit the site and what it must do. WordPress suits content-heavy firms and gives the most flexibility. Design-led brands with simpler needs often do well on a lean WordPress theme. Shopify is our default for e-commerce. Portals and complex features are often custom. We recommend after scoping, and agree in writing who owns the site, code and accounts.

faqs.q: Will the website meet accessibility standards?
faqs.a: We build to WCAG 2.2 AA, which is the standard most UK organisations work to, and test with keyboard navigation, screen readers and contrast checks. That helps you meet the Equality Act 2010 and makes the site easier for everyone to use. Your content team gets guidance on keeping new pages accessible.

faqs.q: Can you build a client portal for a law firm?
faqs.a: Yes. We have built a portal for a US law firm with secure logins, document exchange and online payments. For London firms we add the SRA requirements, UK GDPR controls on document retention and access, and integration with your practice management system where it offers an API.

faqs.q: Do you look after websites after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Website care covers updates, security monitoring, backups, uptime checks and small content changes each month, with one lead to call. We have cleaned up compromised law-firm websites, so we take patching seriously. You always have access to what we build and run for you, so taking the site in-house later is straightforward.

faqs.q: How long does a London website project take?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of templates, the content and any integrations. A focused company site is a much shorter project than an e-commerce store or a portal. We agree the launch date and every milestone in writing before work starts, and we flag risks to those dates early.
